analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.nobodyOnSite: Nobody on the site in the last 5 minutes

analytics.audienceBlurb: The headline tiles — how many people came, how much they looked at, and how many are here right now.
analytics.audienceVisitorsD: Distinct people in the selected period. A visitor is a privacy-friendly daily hash of IP and browser — no cookies — so the same person on two days counts twice.
analytics.audiencePageviewsD: Every page load, including SPA route changes. One visitor can rack up many pageviews, so this is always higher than visitors.
analytics.audienceSessionsD: A visit — one or more pageviews with no 30-minute gap. A returning visitor later in the day starts a fresh session.
analytics.audienceLiveD: Distinct visitors active in the last five minutes, updated as the page refreshes. The 'Right now' panel lists the pages they're on.
analytics.behaviorBlurb: How engaged visits are, and what people do once they arrive — the Pages, Engagement and Clicks tabs.
analytics.behaviorBounceD: Share of sessions that left after a single pageview without interacting. Lower is usually better — the delta arrow is coloured accordingly.
analytics.behaviorAvgSessionD: Average visible time across a whole visit. A backgrounded tab doesn't count, so this is real attention time, not just tab-open time.
analytics.behaviorTimePageT: Avg. time on page / Pages per session
analytics.behaviorTimePageD: How long a single page holds attention, and how many pages a typical visit touches. Higher pages-per-session means people explore more.
analytics.behaviorPagesD: Your most-viewed pages, plus where visits begin (entry) and where they end (exit). Click a row to filter every number to that page.
analytics.behaviorEngagementD: Scroll depth and landing performance, a traffic heatmap by hour and weekday, and which CTAs get clicked and where on the page.
analytics.acquisitionBlurb: Where visitors come from — the Sources, Geography and Technology tabs.
analytics.acquisitionChannelsD: Channels group traffic into Direct, Organic, Social and Paid; Referrers name the exact sites sending it. Click a referrer to filter by it.
analytics.acquisitionUtmD: Traffic tagged with campaign parameters, so you can measure a specific push separately from everything else.
analytics.acquisitionGeoD: A world map shaded by volume, plus ranked countries and browser languages — useful for deciding what to translate.
analytics.acquisitionTechD: Browsers, operating systems, devices and screen sizes. A surprise here — lots of an old browser, say — can explain layout complaints.
analytics.conversionBlurb: Whether visits turn into the outcomes you care about — the Goals, Events, Funnel, Retention and Errors tabs.
analytics.conversionGoalsD: Completion rates for the actions you've defined as goals — the share of visitors doing the thing that matters.
analytics.conversionEventsD: Custom events fired via rta.track(), with their totals and any revenue value summed across them.
analytics.conversionFunnelD: A step-by-step path you define. Each step shows how many sessions reached it and where people drop off.
analytics.conversionRetentionD: Weekly cohorts and how many visitors come back over the following weeks — a read on whether the product holds people.
analytics.conversionErrorsD: Client-side errors the tracker forwarded, so a broken page shows up here rather than only in complaints.
